surfaces.name: agent-manager terminal UI on tmux (macOS, Linux, Windows via psmux or WSL2)
agent-manager subcommands, headless serve and stdio MCP server

claims.answer: Terminal UI (not a GUI) that runs on macOS, Linux and Windows (psmux or WSL2), plus a CLI and stdio MCP server; no browser, phone app or editor extension.

desktop_os.answer: Release v0.49.0 ships darwin, linux and windows archives for amd64 and arm64; README says macOS, Linux, native Windows with psmux, and WSL2.

mobile_apps.answer: No iOS or Android app in the release or source; phone access is only a roadmap item with status Later.

browser.answer: No web client; the product is a terminal UI.

cli.answer: agent-manager subcommands (spawn, send, read, wait, kill, revive, task, settings, export, serve, mcp) with --json output.

editor_extensions.answer: No editor extension; o and F3 open a directory in a chosen editor.

task_actions.answer: Start (n form, quick prompt), steer (space, focus), answer approvals by typing into the pane, review diffs with line comments, revive and resume sessions.

notifications.answer: Native banners on macOS, Linux and WSL toasts, terminal escapes in Ghostty/cmux, and a notify_command for push services.

cross_device_continuity.answer: Sessions live in tmux on the host and another machine's manager can list them over SSH; there is no phone or second-device client.

limitations: Terminal-only; no mobile or browser access (phone access is only a Later roadmap item); Windows needs psmux or WSL2; remote hosts must be Linux or macOS.

claims.answer: Thirteen built-in coding CLIs (Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Grok Build, Gemini CLI, Antigravity CLI, Pi, Command Code, Hermes Agent, Muse Code, Oh My Pi, Cursor CLI, Kiro CLI) plus a shell tab, run as real CLIs in tmux; no custom adapter.

harnesses.answer: Thirteen named CLIs, each with launch, revive, fork, MCP registration and status rules built in.

model_providers.answer: Model, effort and profile lists are read from each CLI at spawn time (SDK initialize, codex app-server, ACP, models commands); Kiro and Command Code offer none.

custom_adapters.answer: Configuration docs say [tools.<name>] blocks have no effect and every CLI definition is built in; unlisted CLIs are feature requests.

session_integration.answer: Launches each CLI in a tmux pane and observes it through hooks (Claude), pane rules, session stores and MCP; asks some CLIs for model lists over their own protocols; does not embed a harness.

mixed_harness_operation.answer: Sessions of different CLIs run side by side in one list and can delegate to each other through MCP.

limitations: CLI rules ship in the binary; an unlisted CLI needs a feature request; model and effort lists exist only for CLIs that expose them.

claims.answer: Each session launches the user's own installed CLI with their login, subscription and config; environment profiles let a session use another config directory or API key.

agent_subscriptions.answer: README: each session launches your own installed tool as-is with your login and subscription.

api_accounts.answer: Environment profiles export variables such as an API key or CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR before the CLI starts.

vendor_credits.answer: No vendor credits or account exist.

local_models.answer: No local-model routing; a CLI that supports local models uses its own settings.

account_switching.answer: Named environment profiles are picked per session, per group default or at spawn (--env) to run a second account or config directory.

provider_restrictions.answer: Provider restrictions are documented by each model provider, outside the repository.

limitations: Credentials stay with each CLI; environment profile values are stored unencrypted in state.db and included in exports.
claims.unknownReason: Provider terms on subscription use through third-party launchers are outside the repository.

claims.answer: Install by Homebrew, Scoop, script or archive; a first-run setup walks through CLIs, layout and theme; then n or space starts an agent in any directory (no Git needed) or a Git repo; SSH connections add remote hosts.

first_task_setup.answer: First-run setup then space or n; install steps for Homebrew, Scoop, scripts and archives.

no_git.answer: A directory that is not a git repo spawns a plain session; the worktree toggle reads unavailable.

local_git_without_remote.answer: Worktree base falls back to a local main, master or HEAD when no remote exists.

hosted_git.answer: Worktrees start from the remote default branch with a throttled fetch; upstream and origin fork layouts are handled.

prerequisite_guidance.answer: Install docs list tmux 3.1+, git and psmux for Windows; the installer offers package-manager commands.

byo_vps_onboarding.answer: C adds an SSH connection to a host that already has agent-manager and starts a headless manager there; it does not provision or install it.

limitations: Needs tmux 3.1+ (psmux on Windows) and git; no managed cloud; remote hosts must already run agent-manager.

claims.answer: Subcommands with --json, a versioned snapshot, headless serve, and a stdio MCP server expose spawn, read, send, wait, kill, revive, archive, move, tasks, terminals and review declarations; no HTTP API, SDK or inbound webhook.

cli.answer: agent-manager spawn, send, read, wait, kill, delete, revive, archive, move, task, settings, env, export, serve and more.

api.answer: snapshot --json and --json outputs are scriptable; there is no HTTP or socket API.

mcp_server.answer: agent-manager mcp serves about thirty tools over stdio and is registered into each MCP-capable CLI session at launch.

webhooks.answer: notify_command runs a shell command per notification (for example curl to ntfy); there is no inbound webhook.

operations.answer: Create (spawn, create_session), inspect (list, read, snapshot), steer (send, type), stop (kill), and review declarations are available from the CLI and MCP.

authentication.answer: The MCP server identifies the calling session from its environment or process tree; callers with no session get a restricted guardrail; nothing uses tokens.

stability.answer: The snapshot envelope and CLI protocol carry versions and refuse mismatches; there is no stated API stability or deprecation policy.

limitations: Local and SSH only; authentication is caller detection, not tokens; no HTTP endpoint.

claims.answer: agent-manager is not an MCP client or plugin host; it registers its own MCP server into each CLI. Plugins are only a Next roadmap item.

mcp_client.answer: The manager is not an MCP client; the launched CLIs manage their own MCP configuration.

plugins.answer: No plugin system; plugins and a marketplace are a roadmap item with status Next.

custom_tools.answer: No custom tool mechanism; saved prompts and environment profiles are not tools.

instructions_import.answer: Saved prompts store named instructions reused in forms, quick prompt and sessions; no import of instruction files.

authentication.answer: MCP registration uses each CLI's own mcp add or config files; the server has no authentication.

permission_scope.answer: Destructive terminal operations are scoped to the caller's own nested terminals and tool calls are annotated; there is no per-integration permission scope.

integration_owner.answer: Each CLI owns its MCP client; the manager registers its server with a CLI-specific mechanism per tool.

limitations: No plugin system; MCP servers, skills and instruction files belong to each launched CLI.

claims.answer: Go terminal UI built on Bubble Tea over a private tmux server; not a GUI desktop, web or mobile client.

desktop_implementation.answer: Go with Bubble Tea and lipgloss rendering in the user terminal, with tmux as the session layer.

implementation_evidence.answer: go.mod and docs/architecture.md at the pinned commit.

limitations: Terminal rendering depends on the host terminal; no web or mobile implementation.

claims.answer: Prompts start sessions from the quick prompt or n form and a shared task list holds work items created from CLI or MCP; no external tracker integration.

local_creation.answer: agent-manager task create or the MCP task tool adds work to the local list.

prompt_intake.answer: Quick prompt (space) and the n form take a first prompt and spawn an agent.

external_import.answer: No external tracker integration or sync.

chat_git_triggers.answer: No external tracker integration or sync.

authoritative_tracker.answer: No external tracker integration or sync.

stable_ids.answer: Tasks and sessions have stable ids in state.db.

sync.answer: No external tracker integration or sync.

supported_edits.answer: Create, claim, finish, release and delete; no edit of title or body.

external_roundtrips.answer: No external tracker integration or sync.

limitations: No import from GitHub, Linear or Jira; tasks have no sync.

claims.answer: Task entries carry a title and body, but there are no plans, acceptance criteria, revisions or editors; tasks persist across restarts.

plans.answer: A task has a title and body.

acceptance_criteria.answer: No plan feature beyond task title and body.

editors.answer: No plan feature beyond task title and body.

revisions.answer: No plan feature beyond task title and body.

implementation_links.answer: A claimed task records its owner session.

amendment.answer: Tasks can be created, released or deleted while others run.

restart_persistence.answer: Tasks persist in SQLite across restarts.

limitations: A task body is free text; no revisions.

claims.answer: Tasks depend on other tasks (depends_on, blocked_by) with readiness and claim enforcement, and sessions nest in unlimited-depth groups; there are no epics.

hierarchy.answer: Groups nest to unlimited depth and terminals nest under agents; tasks are flat.

blockers.answer: depends_on lists blockers; blocked_by shows unfinished ones.

readiness.answer: claim without an id takes the oldest unblocked pending task.

enforcement.answer: ClaimTask refuses a blocked task in a single guarded write.

state_propagation.answer: finish marks done and unblocks dependents.

workflow_constraints.answer: No rigid workflow is required; every tool is registered regardless of coordination mode.

limitations: No epics or task hierarchy; groups organise sessions, not work.

claims.answer: Saved prompts store reusable instructions, sessions keep conversation ids and review state across restarts; agents load their own instruction and skill files; no memory layer.

instructions.answer: Saved prompts up to 64 KiB, name unique, used on spawn, quick prompt and focused sessions.

skills.answer: The repository ships agent-manager skill files for agents; the manager does not manage skills.

project_docs.answer: No managed memory, skills or project-doc layer.

memory.answer: No managed memory, skills or project-doc layer.

scope.answer: Saved prompts are global to the profile.

provenance.answer: No managed memory, skills or project-doc layer.

correction.answer: Saved prompts can be edited or deleted.

deletion.answer: Saved prompts and sessions can be deleted; a session delete removes its worktree when clean.

freshness.answer: No managed memory, skills or project-doc layer.

takeover_continuity.answer: Sessions, groups, messages and review marks persist in state.db and conversations revive by id on the same machine.

limitations: No shared memory, skills or project docs managed by the product.

claims.answer: No code index or retrieval; ctrl+v pastes clipboard images into quick prompt and new-session prompts as file-path chips.

multimodal_inputs.answer: Image paste chips saved under agent-manager-pastes and swapped for paths on send.

limitations: Images are passed as temp file paths and cleared after seven days.

claims.answer: A shared task list (title, body, owner, pending/claimed/done, dependencies) is reachable from CLI and MCP and is not shown in the TUI; there are no labels, priorities, comments or board.

create.answer: Create tasks with title, body and dependencies.

edit.answer: Not part of the task list.

discuss.answer: Not part of the task list.

prioritize.answer: Not part of the task list.

label.answer: Not part of the task list.

assign.answer: Claim assigns the task to the claiming session; no assignment to others.

search.answer: Not part of the task list.

filter.answer: task list shows state, owner and blockers.

archive.answer: Not part of the task list.

reopen.answer: release returns a claimed task to pending.

project_epic_views.answer: Not part of the task list.

idea_parking.answer: A task can be created without starting any agent.

explicit_dispatch.answer: Dispatch is by an agent claiming; there is no human dispatch action.

task_session_separation.answer: Tasks and sessions are separate entities; a task records an owner session.

metadata.answer: Title, body, owner session, state, timestamps and dependency ids.

durable_states.answer: pending, claimed and done persist in SQLite.

external_tracker_requirement.answer: No external tracker is required or integrated.

limitations: Minimal task entity; no discussion, labels, priority, search, archive or project views; no TUI view of tasks.

claims.answer: Agents operate the shared task list through the task MCP tool and CLI as the same entities the manager stores: list, create, claim atomically, finish, release, delete, with dependencies; no TUI view for humans.

shared_ids.answer: Task ids are durable and shared across sessions.

read.answer: task list returns state, owner and blocked_by.

create.answer: create takes title, body and depends_on.

update.answer: claim, finish, release and delete change state; there is no field edit.

claim.answer: Atomic claim; the loser is told who holds the task.

assign.answer: Only self-claim, no assignment to another session.

state_changes.answer: claim, finish and release move state.

children.answer: create_session starts a child session; tasks have no children.

results.answer: finish marks done; there is no result field.

human_visibility.answer: agent-manager task list shows tasks to the user; the TUI has no task view.

attribution.answer: Each task records its owner session.

permissions.answer: Any caller as the local user can use the tools; no role model.

conflicts.answer: SQLite serializes writers so two agents cannot both claim a task.

limitations: No human-facing task view in the TUI; attribution is the owner session id; no permissions model beyond the local user.

claims.answer: No persistent product specification feature.
Any number of agent sessions run concurrently as tmux sessions across groups and SSH hosts, with seven visible states and per-status counts; no quota.

concurrent_sessions.answer: Each session is its own tmux session polled every two seconds.

concurrent_tasks.answer: Several sessions can claim different tasks at once.

quotas.answer: No session quota or concurrency cap found.

observed_concurrency.answer: No published concurrency measurements; not listed on ADEMark.

status_visibility.answer: Rows show working, waiting, finished, errored, idle, dead and starting with group counts and an attention filter.

limitations: No stated concurrency limits; measured concurrency is not published.
claims.unknownReason: Measured concurrency is a benchmark fact not in the repository; this catalog does not run products.

claims.answer: Agents claim tasks atomically, spawn sessions with a first prompt, and queue messages to others; file reservations warn of overlap; humans assign by starting sessions.

human_assignment.answer: Humans start sessions in groups; no assignment to named people.

agent_assignment.answer: create_session starts another agent on a named task.

claims.answer: Atomic task claim.

queues.answer: The task list and the session message queue.

routing.answer: A spawn inherits the caller's CLI, group and directory; no routing engine.

duplicate_prevention.answer: A claimed task cannot be claimed twice and a conversation id cannot be held by two rows.

ownership_enforcement.answer: Task claims are enforced in the database; file reservations are advisory and expire.

limitations: No assignment to humans; file reservations are advisory.

claims.answer: Product-supplied MCP and CLI tools let an agent spawn other agent CLIs (with chosen model, effort and worktree), message them with gated delivery, read their screens and wait for them; no formal role objects.

roles.answer: Callers and spawned sessions are linked by parent_id; there are no named roles (an orchestrator preset is a Later roadmap item).

model_harness_effort.answer: create_session takes CLI, model, effort, profile and environment.

messages.answer: send_session queues a message delivered when the target is at rest, with status tracking.

results_return.answer: read_session returns the target screen and wait_for_session reports its state; no structured result.

cross_harness.answer: Any built-in CLI can spawn or message any other.

orchestration_owner.answer: The manager ships the tools; the coordinating agent is whichever session calls them.

activation.answer: Registered at spawn for MCP-capable CLIs; the coordination setting picks on request or proactive.

authentication.answer: No tokens; the caller is detected from environment or process tree.

live_progress.answer: read_session, list_sessions and status rows show live progress.

retained_results.answer: A stopped session keeps its last screen.

followup.answer: send_session, revive and resume reopen finished work.

invocation.answer: MCP tools or the equivalent CLI subcommands.

limitations: Results return as screens and states, not structured outputs; no authentication between agents.

claims.answer: No scheduler or event triggers; headless serve keeps message delivery and after-turn actions running without the TUI; lifecycle hooks are a Next roadmap item.

schedules.answer: No scheduler, trigger or retry feature.

events.answer: notify_command fires on waiting, errored and optionally finished transitions; it only notifies.

recurring_tasks.answer: No scheduler, trigger or retry feature.

completion_conditions.answer: wait_for_session and archive_self or kill_self after a turn ends express completion.

scheduler_location.answer: No scheduler, trigger or retry feature.

overlaps.answer: No scheduler, trigger or retry feature.

retries.answer: No scheduler, trigger or retry feature.

client_independence.answer: Queued messages and after-turn actions run in a headless manager started with serve.

limitations: A script or cron job can call agent-manager spawn, which is user-assembled rather than a product trigger.

claims.answer: Steer by quick prompt or focus, stop with kill (row kept), revive on the same conversation, waiting and errored notifications with the agent's question quoted; no pause or escalation routing.

pause.answer: No pause control; Ctrl+C reaches the agent as cancel.

stop.answer: x kills a session keeping its row and last screen; kill_session does the same.

resume.answer: v revives resuming the exact conversation by id.

steer.answer: Quick prompt types into a session without attaching; focus passes keys to the agent.

notifications.answer: One banner per waiting or errored transition, plus optional finished and notify_command.

pending_decisions.answer: waiting covers dialogs, permission asks and plain-text questions; the banner quotes the question; w filters.

escalation.answer: notify_command can forward to a phone or chat; there is no routing.

visible_errors.answer: errored state with usage-limit and provider-error rules.

chat_terminal_parity.answer: The agent terminal is the only surface, so questions asked there are detected as waiting.

retained_history.answer: Dead and archived sessions keep their last screen and conversation id.

limitations: No pause control; escalation is a notify_command.

claims.answer: A rail of groups and sessions with per-status counts, an attention filter, waiting-first state marks, fleet CPU and RAM and per-session readings; no epics or dependency graph.

fleet_fixture.answer: Groups with folded per-status counts across local and SSH rows.

parent_child.answer: Terminals nest under agents and groups nest in groups.

attention.answer: waiting, finished and errored are marked and w filters to them.

workload.answer: Header shows agents total CPU and RAM; each session line shows its own.

navigation_errors.answer: errored rows are marked; no error-only filter beyond attention.

fixture_mode.answer: Not applicable; there is no fixture mode.

limitations: Task dependencies are not shown in the TUI; no epic view.

claims.answer: Quick prompt starts an agent in two keystrokes with no preset; model, effort and profile can be chosen per spawn by humans or agents; no natural-language configuration or role views.

presets.answer: Saved prompts and environment profiles; agent presets are a Later roadmap item.

natural_language.answer: Users can tell an agent to set up review or manage sessions through the MCP tools.

agent_configuration.answer: Model, effort and profile per spawn.

in_run_changes.answer: Messages, restart, kill and revive change a running session.

live_roles.answer: Rows show parent grouping and message counts; no role view.

retained_relationships.answer: Group placement and nested terminals persist.

discoverability.answer: Onboarding tour, ? key map and docs.

limitations: Presets and an orchestrator preset are a Later roadmap item.

claims.answer: Agents run in tmux on the local machine or on a Linux or macOS host the user controls and reaches through an SSH connection, where the remote agent-manager keeps running; no managed cloud.

local.answer: Default: tmux sessions on the local machine.

byo_remote.answer: SSH connections list, create and drive sessions on a user-owned host.

self_hosted.answer: No server component; serve is a headless manager, not a hosted control plane.

hybrid.answer: Local and SSH rows share one list.

provisioning.answer: The first refresh starts serve --background on the host; the user installs agent-manager and keys.

payer.answer: The user pays for their machines and agent subscriptions; the manager is free.

resources.answer: The manager sets no compute resources.

expiry.answer: No lifetime limit; sessions stay until killed or the host restarts.

client_disconnect.answer: Sessions run in tmux on the host and keep going when the manager quits or the connection drops.

other_device_continuation.answer: Another machine's manager can add an SSH connection to the same host and attach; no phone client.

limitations: Remote hosts need agent-manager installed; no vendor cloud; no provisioning.

claims.answer: Shared directory by default; optional git worktree per session (<repo>-worktrees/<name>, branch am/<name>); sessions run as the user in a private tmux server; no container, VM or sandbox.

checkout.answer: Sessions share the chosen directory unless a worktree is requested.

branch.answer: Worktree sessions get branch am/<name> from the detected or group base.

worktree.answer: n form, quick prompt ctrl+t, group default and create_session worktree true.

filesystem.answer: No filesystem boundary beyond worktree directories.

process.answer: A private tmux server (agentmgr) keeps sessions apart from the user's own tmux; not a security boundary.

secrets.answer: Environment profile values are hidden in Settings but stored in state.db.

code_separation.answer: Worktrees keep sessions' edits on separate branches.

security_boundary.answer: None; the docs treat commands as running as the user.

limitations: A worktree separates files only; no process, network or secret boundary.

claims.answer: Sessions survive the manager quitting, ssh drops and manager restarts (tmux); dead rows revive on the exact conversation id when known, otherwise through the CLI picker or --continue; state is in SQLite.

client_disconnect.answer: tmux sessions keep running after the manager quits or the ssh connection drops.

worker_crash.answer: A dead tmux session is marked dead and can be revived.

service_restart.answer: Rows and conversation ids persist in state.db and sessions revive after restart.

transcript_reload.answer: Dead sessions keep their last screen snapshot.

process_reconnect.answer: Attach reconnects to the live tmux session.

task_resume.answer: revive runs the tool's resume-by-id command.

state_reconstruction.answer: The store rebuilds groups, sessions and review state.

context_loss.answer: A session with no captured id falls back to a picker or --continue, which the status line warns may land on another conversation.

duplicate_actions.answer: Message delivery is at most once; agent actions on resume are not guarded.

manual_repair.answer: Pickers, rename and CLI install dialogs cover most repair.

multi_day_continuity.answer: Conversations resume across days from the CLI stores with groups and tasks intact.

limitations: Without a captured conversation id revive may resume the wrong conversation; processes die on host reboot but rows revive.

claims.answer: The manager does not install project dependencies or manage services or ports; it checks that agent CLIs, tmux and git exist and offers vendor installers.

dependencies.answer: Detects missing or old agent CLIs and offers installers; no project dependency install.

secrets.answer: Environment profiles inject variables into a session.

remote_setup.answer: SSH connections run in the login shell; the user installs agent-manager on the host.

automatic_repair.answer: A spawn blocked by a missing CLI offers the vendor installer in a shell tab and retries.

limitations: Project environment setup is left to the agent and user.

claims.answer: No run limits; wait_for_session times out and provider usage-limit banners mark a session errored.

timeouts.answer: wait_for_session and a 15 second notify_command timeout.

retries.answer: SSH refresh retries back off from two seconds to thirty seconds.

provider_failures.answer: limit_line and StopFailure map usage limits and request failures to errored.

limitations: No time, turn, token or spend enforcement.

claims.answer: Per-session status states, last screens, fleet and per-session CPU and RAM, conversation ids and local logs (serve.log, notify-command.log); no usage export or per-task statistics.

logs.answer: serve.log and notify-command.log; pane text is captured for the preview.

failure_reasons.answer: errored from usage-limit, provider-error and tool-error rules.

agent_stats.answer: CPU and RAM per session and fleet total.

time_stats.answer: Session line shows how long a state has held and age.

approval_status.answer: waiting covers dialogs and permission asks.

reconnect_consistency.answer: The poller reconciles against a ledger after stale reads.

performance_method.answer: No benchmark method; not listed on ADEMark.

limitations: No exports or historical statistics.
claims.unknownReason: Performance and responsiveness are benchmark facts the catalog does not measure.

claims.answer: No compute-aware scheduling; host gauges and per-agent process usage are displayed, messages queue with caps, and kill and cancel exist.

cpu_ram.answer: Gauges and per-agent CPU and RAM are shown, not enforced.

backpressure.answer: Message queue and rate caps; no spawn throttling.

host_awareness.answer: Each host's stats are read separately.

recovery.answer: Stale delivery claims are retired and sessions revive.

claims.answer: Single-user local tool; no sharing, comments, presence or co-prompting.
No accounts, roles or SSO; GOVERNANCE.md roles describe repository contributors.

Approvals stay in each agent's own prompts; the manager surfaces waiting dialogs, refuses to type into shells by accident, scopes agent terminal control, and envelopes inter-agent messages with limits.

command.answer: Waiting shows pending command approvals; the agent enforces them.

secret.answer: Environment values are not shown in Settings.

delivery.answer: Inter-agent message envelopes tell recipients that commit, push, merge, publish and delete wait for the user; this is an instruction.

allow.answer: Answer a waiting dialog by typing in the pane.

defaults.answer: Each CLI keeps its own permission defaults.

safer_modes.answer: Confirmation before kill, delete and revive of groups.

enforcement.answer: Message caps and terminal scoping are enforced in code; approvals are not.

actions.answer: Messages and review rounds are recorded with sender and round.

edits.answer: Review drafts and reviewed marks persist.

discussion.answer: Agent messages are stored with delivery status.

cross_session_persistence.answer: state.db persists sessions, review state, inbox and tasks.

export.answer: export covers settings, presets, groups and connections only.

mutability.answer: Local rows can be deleted or edited by the user.

claims.answer: ctrl+r opens full-file diffs (unified or side-by-side) with scopes, commit rail, per-file reviewed marks, line comments sent to the agent as numbered rounds and agent-marked handled status; no review queue or ship action.

pending_reviews.answer: Review opens per session; w and the footer surface sessions that finished.

change_understanding.answer: Whole-file context with syntax highlighting and tinted changed lines.

evidence_navigation.answer: Files, change jumps, scope cycle, commit rail, repo and worktree pickers.

comments.answer: Draft line comments with persistent status.

request_changes.answer: C sends drafts as one numbered review prompt to the agent.

missed_evidence.answer: Reviewed marks per scope and outdated flags for comments whose code moved.

narrow_screen.answer: Short windows scroll; layout adapts to terminal size.

context_switching.answer: Comments and reviewed marks return after restart.

roles.answer: An agent can declare repo, base and scope through the review tool.

retained_context.answer: Review state is saved per session and scope.

reviewer_outputs.answer: Review rounds persist with comment ids and status.

revision_links.answer: Commit scope and branch target bind reviews to revisions; outdated comments are flagged.

persistence.answer: Review state and last screens persist.

claims.answer: Everything runs on the user's machines with no required vendor service; state is in SQLite and configuration exports as JSON; sessions, tasks and review state are not exported.

self_hosting.answer: Single binary plus tmux; the only vendor-hosted calls are update and message-feed GETs.

vendor_dependencies.answer: None required; GitHub is used for update checks and the feed.

export.answer: export writes settings, presets, groups and connections as JSON.

import.answer: import merges that JSON by name; sessions and tasks are not restored.

formats.answer: JSON export and a SQLite state.db.

claims.answer: SECURITY.md lists exactly what is touched: local SQLite state, generated agent config, and two unauthenticated GETs at startup and every ten minutes with no version, token or session data; code and prompts go only to the agent CLIs the user runs.

code_data.answer: Code stays local except where the launched CLI sends it.

prompts.answer: Prompts go to the agent; saved prompts and messages live in local state.db.

credentials.answer: Environment profile values are stored in state.db and not redacted in exports.

logs.answer: Local serve.log and an owner-only notify-command.log.

artifacts.answer: Local review state and pasted images in temp.

retention.answer: Pasted images are cleared after seven days; other state persists until deleted.

deletion.answer: Sessions, groups and prompts can be deleted; no data-wipe command is documented.

training.answer: The manager has no model; training use belongs to the agent providers.

subprocessors.answer: No vendor service; provider subprocessors are outside the repository.

telemetry_disclosure.answer: SECURITY.md Network section documents each request and its headers.

telemetry_defaults.answer: No analytics client; update and feed checks are on by default and carry no identifiers.

telemetry_controls.answer: No setting that disables the update and feed requests was found.

consent_prompt.answer: No consent prompt for the update and feed checks.

provider_separation.answer: The manager never calls model providers; it talks to local CLIs only.

limitations: No setting found that disables update and feed requests; provider data handling is each vendor's policy.

evidence.title: agent-manager README
evidence.finding: Local terminal app over tmux running thirteen coding CLIs side by side with live status, quick prompt, worktrees, diff review, MCP delegation between agents, SSH connections; macOS, Linux, Windows via psmux and WSL2; Apache-2.0; cost tracking not here yet.

evidence.title: Usage guide
evidence.locator: Keys; Quick prompt mode; Worktree sessions; Killing and reviving; MCP; Diff review; Groups; SSH connections; Status; Notifications; Stats
evidence.finding: Reference for every key, session lifecycle, worktrees, revive by conversation id, MCP tools, review comments, status states, notification command and host stats.

evidence.title: Configuration guide
evidence.locator: Export and import; Agent CLIs; Key bindings
evidence.finding: Settings live in SQLite state.db; export and import of settings, presets, groups and connections as JSON; per-CLI notes; all CLI rules are built into the binary.

evidence.title: Architecture
evidence.finding: Go packages: Bubble Tea UI, sessioncmd, mcpserver, store (SQLite), tmux driver, status classifier, poller; delivery is at most once.

evidence.title: SSH connections
evidence.finding: A connection lists another host's agent-manager sessions; control flows over ssh batch mode to the remote CLI; remote manager keeps running headless via serve --background.

evidence.title: Install guide
evidence.finding: Installers for macOS, Linux and Windows; requires tmux 3.1+ (psmux 3.4+ on Windows) and git.

evidence.title: Security policy
evidence.finding: Documents generated agent config, stdio MCP server scoped to the caller session, local SQLite state, and the two unauthenticated GET requests at startup and every 10 minutes (releases and message feed).

evidence.title: Governance
evidence.finding: Single maintainer with collaborators; roadmap board; code-owner review enforced.

evidence.title: Apache License 2.0
evidence.finding: Apache License, Version 2.0.

evidence.title: agent-manager v0.49.0 release
evidence.finding: Assets for darwin, linux and windows on amd64 and arm64 plus checksums.txt, install.sh and install.ps1; published 2026-11-14.

evidence.title: GitHub repository metadata
evidence.finding: 699 stars, Apache-2.0, last push 2026-11-16, created 2026-07-15, homepage agent-manager.dev; repository previously at YoanWai/agent-manager.

evidence.title: agent-manager site llms.txt
evidence.finding: Describes a Go TUI on tmux for running thirteen coding CLIs, local developer tool, not a hosted service; no pricing.

evidence.title: Go module
evidence.finding: Go module with Bubble Tea, lipgloss, modernc.org/sqlite, go-sdk for MCP and gopsutil; no HTTP server framework.

evidence.title: Built-in CLI definitions
evidence.finding: Launch, resume, fork, MCP registration and status rules for the thirteen CLIs are compiled into the binary.

evidence.title: MCP server
evidence.finding: stdio MCP server with rename, review, list_sessions, create_session, read_session, send_session, message_status, wait_for_session, revive/kill/archive/move/delete_session, task, reserve_files, groups and terminal tools, report_issue.

evidence.title: Task and reservation tables
evidence.finding: SQLite tables for a shared task list with owner, state pending/claimed/done and dependencies, advisory file reservations with expiry, and an inbox for agent messages.

evidence.title: Task claim
evidence.finding: Claim is one guarded write that refuses a blocked or already claimed task; ClaimNextTask takes the oldest unblocked pending task.

evidence.title: task subcommands
evidence.finding: CLI task list, create (with --depends-on), claim, finish, release and delete run as the caller session.

evidence.title: Agent messages
evidence.finding: Messages are queued rather than typed at once, capped at 8000 bytes with queue and per-sender rate caps and a fingerprint to stop loops.

evidence.title: Spawn path
evidence.finding: One spawn path for form, quick bar, CLI and MCP: opens the requested worktree, launches, hands the worktree back on failure.

evidence.title: Worktree creation
evidence.finding: Creates <repo>-worktrees/<name> on branch am/<name> from the detected base.

evidence.title: Claude Code status hooks
evidence.finding: Generated --settings file makes Claude Code write lifecycle state into a per-session status file read ahead of pane rules.

evidence.title: Status classifier
evidence.finding: Per-tool regex rules over the visible pane classify working, waiting, finished, errored, idle, dead, starting.

evidence.title: Poller
evidence.finding: UI-free poller captures panes every two seconds, delivers messages, runs notifications and after-turn archive or kill.

evidence.title: tmux driver
evidence.finding: Sessions run on a private tmux server named agentmgr; a control-mode client streams the focused pane.

evidence.title: Remote host driver
evidence.finding: Drives another host's agent-manager CLI over ssh with BatchMode and ControlMaster; starts serve --background there.

evidence.title: Update check
evidence.finding: Reads GitHub Releases for newer versions and in-place self-update with checksum verification.

evidence.title: Message feed
evidence.finding: Fetches docs/messages.json from raw.githubusercontent.com on main for in-app notices.

evidence.title: Release and feed ticks
evidence.finding: Checks run at startup and every 10 minutes while open.

evidence.title: Review mode
evidence.finding: Full-file diffs with scopes uncommitted, branch target, commit, staged; draft comments, numbered rounds sent to the agent, reviewed marks per scope persisted in SQLite.

evidence.title: notify command
evidence.finding: User shell command run for each notification with AM_* environment, 15 second timeout, logged on failure.

evidence.title: Environment profiles
evidence.finding: Named environment variable sets stored in state.db and exported in the pane before the CLI starts.

evidence.title: snapshot --json
evidence.finding: Machine-readable list of sessions, terminals, groups and whether a manager runs; versioned envelope.

evidence.title: Host stats
evidence.finding: CPU, memory, swap, disk, battery, network and temperature gauges, plus per-agent process tree CPU and RAM.

evidence.title: agent-manager skill
evidence.finding: Skill file that teaches an agent the spawn, status, answer and review procedure.

evidence.title: Roadmap: Cost and usage tracking
evidence.finding: Status Later: per session and group tokens, cost and plan limits across CLIs; today only CPU and RAM.

evidence.title: Roadmap: Phone access
evidence.finding: Status Later: check on and answer agents from a phone, native app or terminal over SSH, details open.

evidence.title: Roadmap: Plugins and a plugin marketplace
evidence.finding: Status Next: plugins from a marketplace of verified plugins, open questions pending spikes.

evidence.title: Roadmap: Lifecycle hooks
evidence.finding: Status Next: run user commands on session start, state change, archive, task claim or review round; replaces notify_command.

evidence.title: Roadmap: Agent presets and orchestration
evidence.finding: Status Later: save an agent setup as a preset; one preset is an orchestrator that plans work and starts other sessions.

evidence.title: Bounded search: other clients
evidence.locator: grep over internal and main.go for http.ListenAndServe, net.Listen, websocket, electron, ios, android, vscode, jetbrains, webview
evidence.finding: No web server, browser or phone client, native GUI or editor extension; the editor key only launches an editor.

evidence.title: Bounded search: other harnesses and custom adapters
evidence.locator: grep over internal/config and docs/configuration.md for custom tool, [tools.], aider, generic adapter
evidence.finding: Only the thirteen built-in CLIs plus a shell tab; configuration docs say [tools.<name>] blocks have no effect and unlisted CLIs are feature requests.

evidence.title: Bounded search: schedules and triggers
evidence.locator: grep for cron, schedule, ticker spawn, webhook receiver over internal
evidence.finding: No scheduler, event trigger or inbound webhook; background delivery and after-turn actions run in the poller or headless serve.

evidence.title: Bounded search: collaboration and enterprise
evidence.locator: grep for sso, saml, rbac, organization, invite, presence, multi-user over internal and docs
evidence.finding: No accounts, roles, SSO, shared prompting or presence; one OS user.

evidence.title: Bounded search: container, VM and sandbox
evidence.locator: grep -w for docker, podman, sandbox, seatbelt, bwrap, firejail, qemu over internal
evidence.finding: No container, VM or OS sandbox isolation; sandbox mentions are about Claude Code running inside its own sandbox PID namespace.

evidence.title: Bounded search: cost and limits
evidence.locator: grep for cost, usd, spend, budget, token over internal non-test files
evidence.finding: No cost, spend, budget or token accounting; README states cost tracking is not here yet.

evidence.title: Bounded search: PR and delivery
evidence.locator: grep for gh pr, git push, git commit, merge request over internal non-test files
evidence.finding: No PR creation, commit, push, merge or deploy action; git is used for worktrees, fetch, diffs and cleanup; gh is used only to file issues on the agent-manager repository.

evidence.title: Bounded search: telemetry
evidence.locator: grep for telemetry, analytics, sentry, posthog, mixpanel over internal and docs
evidence.finding: No analytics or crash-reporting client; only the documented update and feed GET requests; telemetry matches are Gemini CLI local telemetry read for conversation ids.

evidence.title: Bounded search: hosted service and pricing
evidence.locator: grep for pricing, billing, subscription, account, sign up over README, docs, internal
evidence.finding: No hosted service, account or pricing; GitHub Sponsors link only.
